what_the_coherent_reading_is: p_lifetime_raw_* from the same lifetime model, read off its monotone quantile function; coherent across horizons by construction; NOT a recalibration

evidence_for_preferring_it.result: isotonic 54 violations vs coherent 0; Brier better at both horizons, p < 0.0001 (cluster bootstrap by launch, 4000 draws)
evidence_for_preferring_it.status: EXPLORATORY: T1 is not a blind window (29 and 64 events); the population differs from this snapshot, which has no outcomes yet

count_calibration_caveat.finding: coherence is not calibration. Summed over the 13,238 uncontrolled objects the coherent reading expects MORE 30-day re-entries than the isotonic one (404.0 vs 229.1 on this snapshot; physics_history 21.6), and on the T1 window it over-predicts observed events by 14.8x [10.2, 23.6] against 10.5x for the isotonic reading and 1.5x for physics_history — while having the better Brier score (0.0026 vs 0.0087)
count_calibration_caveat.consequence: prefer the coherent reading for per-object ordering and horizon consistency; do not read either lifetime variant as a calibrated expected count. The twin's reported forecast uses physics_history for uncontrolled objects, which is the variant closest to observation

scope_note: L17 concerns the lifetime-variant columns only. The twin's reported forecast p_30d/p_90d/p_1yr is a gated mixture and has 0 violations; the top-50 ranking uses p_30d and is unaffected.
